classification.classification_note: ASan reports `negative-size-param` because `expand_include()` strips a lone leading quote, underflows the include-path length from 1 to `(size_t)-1`, truncates that value to signed `len == -1`, and passes it to `memcpy()`. The unsafe copy would then read from the attacker-controlled token buffer through an advanced source pointer.

bug_description.normalized: The staged sudoers witness is noisy, but the raw file ends at EOF with `@includedir \"` and no trailing newline. Vulnerable `sudoers_input()` at `plugins/sudoers/toke.l:1297-1308` appends the missing newline before lexing, so the parser actually sees a final `@includedir \"\n` line. In `plugins/sudoers/toke.l`, the `GOTINC` rule then accepts the two-byte token `\"`; `fill_txt()` collapses that escape and materializes `sudoerslval.string` as the one-character string `"`. The parser reduces that line through the `includedir` production and `sudoersparse()` calls `push_include($1, true)`, which passes `strlen(opath) == 1` into `expand_include()`. `expand_include()` strips any leading double quote whenever `*opath == '"'`, without requiring a matching trailing quote or even `olen >= 2`: for this witness it advances `opath` to the terminating NUL and underflows `olen` from 1 to `(size_t)-1`. The helper then assigns that underflowed value to signed `int len`, which becomes `-1` on the reproduced run; `path = pp = rcstr_alloc(len + dirlen)` still returns a non-NULL destination buffer on the crashing execution, and the observed `subst == false` branch reaches `memcpy(pp, opath, len)`. AddressSanitizer reports `negative-size-param (size=-1)` at `expand_include`. The fix removes the caller-supplied length, recomputes `strlen(opath)` inside `expand_include()`, strips quotes only when both ends are `"` and `olen > 1`, rejects the empty result, and widens `len` and `dirlen` to `size_t`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled include path on the crashing path. After `sudoers_input()` normalizes the unterminated final line, the `GOTINC` lexer rule consumes the raw token `\"` and stores it as `sudoerslval.string` for the parser.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` ends at EOF with raw bytes `@includedir \"` and no trailing newline. `sudoers_input()` appends that newline before lexing; at line 738 `sudoerstext` is therefore the two-byte sequence `\"`, and the `fill` macro expands to `fill_txt`, which allocates a 3-byte buffer and collapses the escape so the stored string becomes the one-character path `"`.

tainted_value_origin.code: dst = olen ? realloc(sudoerslval.string, olen + len + 1) : malloc(len + 1);
tainted_value_origin.description: ASan allocation origin for the include-path token buffer that later becomes `opath`. On the witness line `@includedir \"`, `fill_txt()` allocates 3 bytes for the two-byte token plus terminator; its copy loop then strips the backslash and leaves the stored string as just `"`.

root_cause.description: Incomplete quote-stripping guard. `expand_include()` strips a leading double quote without checking that the path is at least two bytes long and also ends with `"`.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed one-byte string `"`, this block advances `opath` to the terminating NUL and underflows `olen` from 1 to `(size_t)-1`. The fix changes this exact logic to `if (olen > 1 && opath[0] == '"' && opath[olen - 1] == '"')` and returns `NULL` when the post-strip length is zero.

sink.description: ASan sink. After the quote-strip underflow, `opath` points at the terminating NUL inside the token buffer, `path = pp = rcstr_alloc(len + dirlen)` has already produced the destination pointer, and the raw-copy arm passes `len == -1` to `memcpy()`.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param (size=-1)` in `expand_include`; the faulting source address is `0x602000000b31`, one byte inside the 3-byte region allocated for the step-1 token buffer, which confirms the crash happened in the raw-copy `memcpy()` arm rather than the `%h` substitution path.

parser_admitted.description: The raw saved file ends with `@includedir \"` at EOF; `sudoers_input()` appends the missing newline before lexing, after which the lexer returns `INCLUDEDIR` and switches to `GOTINC` to read the following path token. The earlier syntax errors reported for unrelated lines do not stop the parser from reaching this final directive.

coarse_trace.summary: The raw file ends with `@includedir \"` at EOF; `sudoers_input()` appends the missing newline, and the lexer materializes the path token `\"` as the one-character string `"`.
The parser reduces that final line through the `includedir` production and calls `push_include($1, true)` with the one-byte path string.

Because the path begins with `"`, `expand_include()` strips a non-existent closing quote, underflows `olen`, truncates it to signed `len == -1`, and still obtains a non-NULL destination buffer from `rcstr_alloc(len + dirlen)`.
The saved crashing execution keeps `subst` false, takes the raw-copy arm, and calls `memcpy(pp, opath, len)` with `opath` advanced into the token buffer and `len == -1`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The raw file ends at EOF with `@includedir \"`, and `sudoers_input()` appends the missing newline before lexing. In `GOTINC` state the lexer then feeds the two-byte token `\"` to `fill()`, and `fill_txt()` allocates a 3-byte buffer and collapses the escape so `sudoerslval.string` becomes the one-character path `"`.

After the final line is reduced as an `includedir` directive, the parser passes the step-1 string to `push_include()` with `isdir = true`. This is the `sudoersparse` frame named in the saved ASan crash stack.
The path handed over from step 2 is exactly `"`, so `strlen(opath)` is 1. `push_include()` passes that one-byte length into `expand_include()` as `olen`.

Root cause. This branch executes for any leading `"`, even when there is no trailing quote and `olen == 1`. On the witness path it advances `opath` to the terminating NUL and underflows `olen` from 1 to `(size_t)-1`.

The helper stores the underflowed `size_t` value from step 4 in signed `int len`. On the reproduced run this conversion yields `len == -1`, which is the negative size reported by ASan at the later `memcpy()` call.

This call produces the destination pointer later used by the sink. In the fuzz target, `init_parser("sudoers", false, true)` leaves `sudoers` without any slash, so the preceding relative-path logic leaves `dirlen == 0`; step 5 therefore reaches `rcstr_alloc()` as `len + dirlen == -1`. In `plugins/sudoers/rcstr.c:56-69`, `rcstr_alloc()` allocates `sizeof(struct rcstr) + len`, so the converted `size_t` value wraps and can still yield a small non-NULL allocation. On the crashing run it returned `rcs->str`, making both `path` and `pp` non-NULL and bypassing the early return.

The saved crash occurs in the `else` arm at line 1084, so this branch condition is false on the reproduced run. That matches the witnessed path data, which contains only the lone quote materialized at step 1 and no `%h` sequence to trigger hostname substitution.

Sink. The raw-copy arm uses the destination pointer from step 6, the advanced source pointer from step 4, and the negative size from step 5. AddressSanitizer intercepts this call as `negative-size-param (size=-1)`; the reported source address is one byte inside the 3-byte buffer allocated for the original `\"` token.

poc.trigger: The saved Stage 01 command `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_30271 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` runs the vulnerable `fuzz_sudoers` target on this exact file and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param (size=-1)` in `expand_include()`.

format.name: malformed sudoers @includedir with lone escaped quote
format.contract: Exactly the staged witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_30271/poc`. The raw saved file ends at EOF with `@includedir \"`; `sudoers_input()` appends the missing newline before lexing, so the parser actually consumes `@includedir \"\n` on the crashing path. The verified trigger semantics are limited to that witnessed raw suffix plus the observed normalization and parsing behavior: the `GOTINC` rule accepts the two-byte token `\"`, `fill_txt()` collapses it to the one-character string `"`, and `push_include()` calls `expand_include()` with `strlen(opath) == 1`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader malformed-include contract beyond this witnessed lone-quote directive; the preceding malformed lines only show that parsing continues far enough to reach the final `@includedir`.
